issues.description: The problem specification and UML declare SealSaloon.checkOrderReady() as a void method, but the solution implementation defines checkOrderReady() with a boolean return type. This mismatch in the method return type can confuse students about the expected signature and behavior (the spec describes a procedure that serves orders and does not mention a return value).
issues.suggestedFix: Align the implementation with the problem statement: change SealSaloon.checkOrderReady() in src/de/tum/cit/ase/SealSaloon.java to return void (remove the boolean return and any return statements). Alternatively, update the problem statement and UML to explicitly state that checkOrderReady() returns a boolean (and document the meaning of the return value). Prefer the first option to match the current specification that describes it as a procedure.
